attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A retrospective factual assertion that the OpenAI Abilene extension was never real. The normalisation matches the statement.

contract.note: Reading 'never existed' as 'never a committed plan' fits his concession that it was only 'supposedly-planned'. A literal 'never discussed' reading would be false, so the result depends on this reading. It is an ordinary reading, not a stretched one.

evidence.note: OpenAI disclosure from Sep 2025. It called the expansion only 'potential', which matches the support condition.
Mar 2026 report: the expansion lease was never finalized, and OpenAI says it only 'considered' expanding before the plan was dropped.
Shows real financing negotiations that failed. This tempers a literal 'never existed' but shows nothing was committed.
Adjacent Microsoft campus announced after the post. A different tenant, so it does not bear on the OpenAI expansion.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's reading (no committed OpenAI expansion), the record supports the claim. OpenAI only ever called it 'potential', the lease was never finalized, and the plan was dropped in March 2026. Real negotiations did happen, which cuts against a literal reading. 'Never going to happen' is about intent and is not scored separately.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'I am certain ... is going to break' is an unhedged forecast, so it is scored. The cause and the compounding factors are kept. 'Near future' gives no fixed deadline.

contract.note: The readings of 'major big tech service', 'prolonged' and attribution to AI-written code are ordinary. The open horizon is handled correctly: absence of an event cannot contradict the claim.

evidence.note: AWS incident of Dec 2025, which Amazon disputes. It predates the post, so it cannot fulfil the forecast.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet has no qualifying prolonged big-tech outage after 2026-03-24 credibly attributed to AI-written code, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Because there is no deadline, the absence of such an event is not a failure. The forecast stays open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Two-part factual assertion: construction lags GPU sales, and those sales accelerate every quarter. Both parts are kept.

contract.note: Using FY2026 Data Center and compute revenue fits his own context. Even the looser reading (sales merely rising each quarter) fails if a quarter declined. 'Dramatically slower' has no measure.

evidence.note: Q2 FY26 compute revenue fell 1% from the prior quarter, so GPU sales did not even rise that quarter.
Q2 FY26 Data Center revenue grew only 5% from the prior quarter. The prior quarter's rate is not in the packet.
Q4 FY26 growth of 22% was below Q3's 25%, so the growth rate slowed, though the dollar increase was larger.
Q3 FY26 Data Center revenue rose 25% from Q2, so growth did speed up that quarter.
Microsoft's CEO says he has GPUs in inventory and no data center shells ready for them. This supports part (a), for one large buyer.

reviews.rationale: Part (a), construction lagging GPU purchases, gets some support from Microsoft's CEO, though from one buyer and unquantified. Part (b), sales accelerating 'every single quarter', is contradicted: compute revenue fell in Q2 FY26, and the growth rate slowed from Q3 to Q4.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A present-tense factual claim that most GPUs sold, by value, are uninstalled. Faithful to the statement.

contract.note: Majority by value, measured just before the post, is an ordinary plain reading of 'mostly sitting'.

evidence.note: Late-2025 Microsoft remark that some GPUs await power. Gives no amount or share, and predates the target period.
Secondhand mid-2026 report of Amazon warehousing GPUs. After the target period and not industry-wide.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows that some GPUs at individual buyers were waiting for power, but nothing measures the share of GPU sales value uninstalled around March 2026. Neither support nor contradiction is established.
